# fold_ranges

fold_ranges(nums) sorts the distinct integers in nums and joins them with commas, writing every run of 3 OR MORE consecutive integers as first-last. Inside a range, a negative endpoint is written in parentheses; outside a range, numbers are written plainly. fold_ranges([]) == "".

Examples:

- `fold_ranges([6, -4, 12, 9, -2]) == '-4,-2,6,9,12'`
- `fold_ranges([-2, 2, 13, -7, 3, -1]) == '-7,-2,-1,2,3,13'`
- `fold_ranges([-1, 2, 7, -5, -7]) == '-7,-5,-1,2,7'`
- `fold_ranges([7, -7, -3, -5, -8, 11, 8, -2, 5, -4]) == '-8,-7,(-5)-(-2),5,7,8,11'`
- `fold_ranges([7, 9, 2, 8]) == '2,7-9'`
- `fold_ranges([-4, -5, 8, 14, -9, 7, 4, 3, -7, -3]) == '-9,-7,(-5)-(-3),3,4,7,8,14'`
- `fold_ranges([-6, 1, 4, 3]) == '-6,1,3,4'`
- `fold_ranges([14, -7, 12, 13, 5]) == '-7,5,12-14'`
- `fold_ranges([-8, 5, 0, 3, 13, -1, 9, 2, 4]) == '-8,-1,0,2-5,9,13'`
- `fold_ranges([7, -1, -8, -4]) == '-8,-4,-1,7'`
- `fold_ranges([3, -4, 10, 12, -2, -1]) == '-4,-2,-1,3,10,12'`
- `fold_ranges([-1, 0, 5, 6, 3, -2, 10]) == '(-2)-0,3,5,6,10'`
